messages:
lia: customer CS-2387 reporting large spike in 5xx/timeouts from hosted API, mostly p95/p99 tail timeouts. they say it started ~2026-03-15T09:02Z. link to ticket: https://redwood/support/CS-2387 :frowning:

samir: ack. any sample request IDs or timestamps we can grep? also is this single-tenant or multi-tenant?

lia: sample req id: req_20260315_09_02_7f3a. tenant=acme-corp (single-tenant). short curl they ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxx' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"longseq-16k","input":"<~8k tokens>"}' \\n  --max-time 30
```
responses: many 504/502, some eventual 200 but with >6s latency.

lia: pasted excerpt from gateway logs around the failures:
```
[2026-03-15T09:02:07Z] gateway INFO enqueue tenant=acme-corp queue_depth=2036 limit=2000
[2026-03-15T09:02:09Z] batcher WARN pending_batch_queue=2120 dequeue_wait=3800ms kv_cache_miss=high
[2026-03-15T09:02:10Z] gateway ERROR reject req=req_20260315_09_02_7f3a reason=enqueue_timeout
[2026-03-15T09:02:10Z] proxy ERROR upstream 5xx code=502 backend=runtime-34
```

alex: that pattern matches a continuous-batcher backlog caused by longseq requests. metrics I pulled for that time window:
```
continuous_batcher.pending_requests.p95 = 2100
continuous_batcher.dequeue_latency.p95 = 4.2s
runtime.kv_cache.miss_rate = 0.78
gateway.enqueue.depth = 2036 (limit 2000)
```
we're seeing queue depth clobber limit, batcher spends long time waiting to fill huge batches, KV cold miss exacerbates latency.

mira: immediate mitigations to avoid client-facing 5xxs:
- enable tenant-level throttling (burst=100/s, sustained=20/s) for acme-corp
- temporarily lower max_batch_wait_ms to 10ms for longseq models so we don't wait to fill huge batches
- route tenant to smaller / cheaper model variant as fallback (model_shortseq-8k) to reduce per-request cost and speed
these are low-risk short-term changes.

samir: on support side I'll ask acme to apply client backoff and disable aggressive retry loops. can you share a one-line repro they can run with exponential backoff suggestion? I'll include it in the message.

lia: repro helper we gave them (bash):
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do 
  (curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
    -d '{"model":"longseq-16k","input":"'$(head -c 9000 /dev/urandom | base64)'"}') &
done
wait
```
this simulates ~50 concurrent longseq requests; reproduces the spike locally for me.

alex: ran the repro in a staging cluster. output snippet:
```
[staging] gateway WARN enqueue depth hit=2012 limit=2000
[staging] batcher ERROR dequeue_timeout reqs=48 evicted=2
[staging] runtime WARN kv_cache_spinup duration=1200ms
[staging] gateway 504 tenant=acme-corp sample_req=req_... tail_latency=6.3s
```
config suggestion that reproduced recovery (not permanent):
```
continuous_batcher.max_queue_depth = 4000
continuous_batcher.max_batch_wait_ms = 12
gateway.tenant_default.throttle = {burst:100,rate:20}
```
note: increasing max_queue_depth prevents immediate rejects but also increases memory and tail latency risk.

mira: exactly — increasing depth is a band-aid. prefer autoscale policy (add more longseq capacity) + small-model fallback + prefix/KV caching to reduce cold misses. also add a short-term rule to convert 504s to 429 for tenants exceeding retry thresholds so clients back off.

ops-bot: ALERT: rate-limit spike detected tenant=acme-corp retries=4520 window=10m threshold=1000 action=notify-ops

samir: billing/customer impact — looks like a retry storm added ~12k token charges in 10 minutes for acme-corp. recommend we proactively issue a one-time credit while they fix client behavior. lia, can you handle the customer comms?

lia: yes — I told them to enable exponential backoff (start 500ms, factor 2, cap 10s) and to reduce concurrency. they applied it and latency/errors dropped within 2 mins. they confirmed reduced retries in CS chat. I'll file the follow-up ticket with billing. :thumbsup:

alex: follow-up action items I'll open:
- create a short runbook entry for longseq-induced batcher backlog + safe mitigations (tmp throttles, fallback routing, autoscale)
- add telemetry alert for kv_cache_miss correlated with pending_batches.p95 > 800
- evaluate faster prefix caching for longseq models
I'll assign to eng-runtime and ops. :eyes:

mira: thanks team. plan: support to confirm customer credit/notes, eng to implement runbook + alert, ops to evaluate autoscale and canary fallback. if this happens again we'll do a postmortem. closing thread after CS update.
